chapterNote: The psalm of the seven thunders — 'the voice of the LORD' sounds seven times as a storm rolls in off the sea. It shatters the cedars of Lebanon, makes the mountains buck like calves, hews lightning out of the sky, sweeps south to the wilderness of Kadesh, strips the forests, and sends the deer into early labor. It opens in heaven, with the sons of the mighty — the angelic court — told to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD, and the storm sequence ends in the temple, where everything answers it with one word: Glory. Scholars have long noticed that this has the shape of a Canaanite storm-hymn — whether borrowed and re-addressed to the LORD or written to answer one — and it is addressed to the God who actually sat enthroned over the Flood and sits as King forever. The last verse is the point of the whole display: the God whose voice does all that gives His strength to His people and blesses them with peace. Jewish liturgy reads it on Pentecost; the church has read it in every storm.

1.text: A psalm of David. Ascribe to the LORD, you sons of the mighty — ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Give [yahab — ascribe] unto the LORD [YHWH], O ye mighty ['ye sons of the mighty', bene elim, the KJV margin]; give unto the LORD glory [kabod] and strength [oz].
1.notes: havu la-YHWH bene elim (H3051, H1121, H410): yahab is 'give, ascribe' — the same imperative Deuteronomy 32:3 uses, 'ascribe ye greatness unto our God' — and the bene elim, sons of the mighty, are the heavenly court (cf. Psalm 89:6): the angels are told to hand God the glory and strength — kabod and oz (H3519, H5797) — that are already His.

2.text: Ascribe to the LORD the glory owed to His name; bow down to the LORD in holy splendor.
2.amp: Give [yahab] unto the LORD [YHWH] the glory ['the honour of his name', kabod, the KJV margin] due unto His name [shem]; worship [shachah — bow down] the LORD in the beauty ['in his glorious sanctuary', hadarah, the KJV margin] of holiness [qodesh].
2.notes: kebod shemo (H3519, H8034): the glory that belongs to the Name — hishtachavu la-YHWH be-hadrat-qodesh (H7812, H1927, H6944): bow in holy adornment — the phrase 1 Chronicles 16:29 and 2 Chronicles 20:21 also use, of worshipers dressed for the sanctuary or of the sanctuary's own splendor; the margin allows both.

3.text: The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders — the LORD, over the vast waters.
3.amp: The voice [qol] of the LORD [YHWH] is upon the waters [mayim]: the God [El] of glory [kabod] thunders [raam]: the LORD is upon many ['great', rav, the KJV margin] waters.
3.notes: qol YHWH (H6963, H3068) — 'the voice of the LORD' will sound seven times in this psalm, the seven thunders. El-ha-kabod hir'im (H410, H3519, H7481): the God of glory thunders, al-mayim rabbim (H4325, H7227) — the storm coming in off the Mediterranean, which is where a Canaanite poet would have put Baal; David puts the LORD there.

4.text: The voice of the LORD comes in power; the voice of the LORD comes in majesty.
4.amp: The voice [qol] of the LORD [YHWH] is powerful ['in power', koach, the KJV margin]; the voice of the LORD is full of majesty ['in majesty', hadar, the KJV margin].
4.notes: qol-YHWH ba-koach, qol-YHWH be-hadar (H6963, H3581, H1926): the margin's 'in power', 'in majesty' — the voice arrives clothed in them. Thunders two and three.

5.text: The voice of the LORD shatters the cedars; yes, the LORD splinters the cedars of Lebanon.
5.amp: The voice [qol] of the LORD [YHWH] breaks [shabar — shatters] the cedars [erez]; yea, the LORD breaks the cedars of Lebanon [Levanon].
5.notes: shober arazim (H7665, H730): the cedars of Lebanon (H3844) were the most prized building timber of the ancient Near East — tall, straight, fragrant, slow to rot, the beams of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 5:6) — and the storm's voice snaps them like kindling. The fourth thunder.

6.text: He makes them skip like a calf — Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox.
6.amp: He makes them also to skip [raqad] like a calf [egel]; Lebanon [Levanon] and Sirion [Siryon] like a young [ben] unicorn [reem — wild ox].
6.notes: va-yarqidem kemo-egel (H7540, H5695): the mountains made to skip like a calf, as in Psalm 114:4 — Lebanon and Sirion (H3844, H8303), Sirion being the Sidonian name for Mount Hermon (cf. Deuteronomy 3:9), like a ben-reemim (H1121, H7214), a young aurochs. The two great northern ranges bucking like livestock.

7.text: The voice of the LORD carves out flames of fire.
7.amp: The voice [qol] of the LORD [YHWH] divides ['cutteth out', chatsab — hews, the KJV margin] the flames [lehabah — lahabot, flames] of fire [esh].
7.notes: qol-YHWH chotseb lahabot esh (H6963, H2672, H3852, H784): chatsab is the quarryman's verb, to hew stone — the thunder-voice hewing lightning out of the sky, the fifth thunder. WEB reads it as lightning-strikes; the picture is the same.

8.text: The voice of the LORD makes the wilderness writhe; the LORD makes the wilderness of Kadesh writhe.
8.amp: The voice [qol] of the LORD [YHWH] shakes [chul — writhes, whirls] the wilderness [midbar]; the LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh [Qadesh].
8.notes: qol YHWH yachil midbar (H6963, H2342, H4057): chul is the writhing of a woman in labor — the desert twisting under the storm — and the storm has now crossed the whole land, from Lebanon in the north to midbar Qadesh (H6946) in the far south. Thunder six.

9.text: The voice of the LORD makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare — and in His temple, all of it says, 'Glory!'
9.amp: The voice [qol] of the LORD [YHWH] makes the hinds [ayalah — does] to calve ['to be in pain', chul, the KJV margin], and discovers [chasaph — strips bare] the forests [yaar]: and in His temple [hekal] does every one ['every whit of it uttereth, etc', amar, the KJV margin] speak of His glory [kabod].
9.notes: The seventh thunder: qol YHWH yecholel ayyalot (H2342, H355) — the same chul as verse 8, the writhing that brings the deer's fawn early — va-yechesoph yearot (H2834, H3295), the forests stripped. Then the answer from the sanctuary: u-be-hekhalo kullo omer kabod (H1964, H559, H3519) — 'in His temple, all of it says: Glory' — the one word the storm was for.

10.text: The LORD sat enthroned over the Flood; the LORD sits enthroned as King forever.
10.amp: The LORD [YHWH] sits [yashab] upon the flood [mabbul — the Deluge]; yea, the LORD sits King [melek] for ever [olam].
10.notes: YHWH la-mabbul yashab (H3999, H3427): mabbul is the Flood narrative's own word for Noah's Flood (Genesis 6-11), and outside Genesis it appears only here — the LORD enthroned over the greatest storm there ever was. va-yeshev YHWH melekh le-olam (H4428, H5769): and He is still sitting. The storm of verses 3-9 is a small one.

11.text: Strength the LORD will give to His people; the LORD will bless His people with peace.
11.amp: The LORD [YHWH] will give [natan] strength [oz] unto His people [am]; the LORD will bless [barak] His people with peace [shalom].
11.notes: YHWH oz le-ammo yitten (H5797, H5971, H5414): the oz, the strength, that the angels ascribed to Him in verse 1 is handed down to His people — YHWH yevarekh et-ammo ba-shalom (H1288, H7965): and after seven thunders, the last word is shalom. The storm passes; the people are left with peace.
